q: What color represents authority and is associated with mourning in some cultures?
n: Black signals authority and formality and is associated with mourning in many cultures. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: Which are the primary pigment colors?
n: The pigment primaries are red, yellow and blue. Mixing pairs of them gives the secondary colours: orange, green and violet. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: Which 1920s center of artistic experimentation still shapes countless consumer products?
n: The Bauhaus (1919–33), a centre of artistic experimentation, still shapes countless consumer products through modern industrial design. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Bauhaus.

q: What term covers buildings mixing historical styles in the 19th and early 20th centuries?
n: Eclecticism covers 19th- and early-20th-century buildings that freely mix historical styles. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Eclecticism.

q: Which fin-de-siècle style has organic, dynamic forms and whiplash curves?
n: Art Nouveau (fin de siècle, about 1890–1910) has organic, dynamic forms and whiplash curves. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Art Nouveau.

q: Which approach is based on open planning free of historical detail?
n: Modernism is based on open planning, function and new materials, free of historical detail. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Modernism.

q: It is independent and stands on its own.
n: "Isolationism" here describes the building conceived as an independent object that stands on its own, apart from its context, the opposite of contextualism. Source: Rowe & Koetter, Collage City (object vs. fabric); Ching.

q: What is considered the origin of architecture?
n: Architecture originated as shelter from weather and the elements. Source: Vitruvius, De Architectura, Book II; Laugier, Essay on Architecture (the primitive hut).

q: Which event turned architecture "modern"?
n: The Industrial Revolution, with new materials (iron, steel, glass) and building types, turned architecture "modern". Source: Frampton, Modern Architecture: A Critical History.

q: Which theory means harmony of parts with the whole and of the building with its site?
n: Organic architecture, Wright's theory, seeks harmony of the parts with the whole and of the building with its site. Source: Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: What style uses raw concrete left unfinished?
n: Brutalism uses raw, unfinished concrete (béton brut). Brutalist buildings show board-marked concrete and massive, sculptural forms, as in Le Corbusier's Unité d'Habitation. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Brutalism.

q: What is the dark part of an object facing away from the light?
n: Shade is the dark part of an object facing away from the light. Shadow is the dark area it casts. Source: Ching, Architectural Graphics.

q: What thinking judges whether statements are true and spots errors?
n: Critical thinking judges whether statements are true and spots errors in reasoning. Source: Ennis, Critical Thinking; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Feng shui is a Chinese practice based on:
n: Feng shui is a Chinese geomantic practice that sites buildings by the perceived forces of the land, water and wind. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, feng shui.

q: What is the creative process of generating, developing and communicating new ideas?
n: Ideation is the creative process of generating, developing and communicating new ideas. Source: Brown, Change by Design (IDEO); Merriam-Webster.

q: Rotating an arch about its central vertical axis forms a:
n: Rotating an arch about its central vertical axis forms a dome. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Rotating a right triangle about its vertical leg forms a:
n: Rotating a right triangle about one leg forms a cone. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: An arch extruded in a straight line forms a:
n: An arch extruded in a straight line forms a barrel vault. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: In perceiving space, the sense of smell matters because it:
o: Helps choose materials that limit bad odors
n: Smell affects how a space is perceived, so designers choose materials and ventilation that limit bad odours. Source: Pallasmaa, The Eyes of the Skin.

q: Which balance places equal elements on either side of a central axis, giving repose and order?
n: Symmetrical (formal) balance places equal elements on either side of a central axis, giving repose and order. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the 1D of sensory experience in design?
n: The item ranks the senses by dominance in design perception: sight first (visual). Source: Pallasmaa, The Eyes of the Skin; Rasmussen, Experiencing Architecture.

q: What is the 2D of sensory experience in design?
n: Second in the item's ranking of the senses is hearing (sounds). Source: Pallasmaa, The Eyes of the Skin; Rasmussen, Experiencing Architecture.

q: What is the 3D of sensory experience in design?
n: Third in the item's ranking of the senses is touch. Touch reveals texture, temperature and material quality through the hands and feet. Source: Pallasmaa, The Eyes of the Skin.

q: What is the 4D of sensory experience in design?
n: Fourth in the item's ranking of the senses is smell. Smell is closely tied to memory and gives places a strong identity. Source: Pallasmaa, The Eyes of the Skin.

q: What is the 5D of sensory experience in design?
n: Fifth in the item's ranking of the senses is taste. Taste is the least used sense in architecture but figures in multisensory design theory. Source: Pallasmaa, The Eyes of the Skin.

q: Removing dead-end corridors is mainly a matter of:
n: Removing dead-end corridors is mainly a circulation and egress matter. The NBC limits dead ends to 6 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: Otherwise called the use of the building.
n: A building's use is its function. Function is the purpose and activities a building serves, which shape its plan and form. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Promotes effective exchange of ideas.
n: Good communication, the effective exchange of ideas, keeps designer, client and team aligned. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice.

q: What is the overall appearance or style of a building that expresses its identity?
n: Architectural character is the overall appearance or style that expresses a building's identity and purpose. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: A design concern that ensures comfort, safety, and usefulness for occupants.
n: Ergonomics is the design concern for occupants' comfort, safety and usefulness. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: The maximum height of shower heads is ___ mm.
n: Shower heads are commonly mounted at a maximum of about 2,000 mm. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design; Panero & Zelnik.

q: The average adult eye level is ___ mm.
n: Average standing adult eye level is about 1,450–1,550 mm. The item's 1,450 mm suits Filipino stature. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space; Philippine anthropometric data.
